subject: Discovery recap — recommended models, schema tests, and next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Ana Morales <ana@storlytics.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.k@storlytics.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T15:00:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap — recommended models, schema tests, and next steps

Hi Ana / Samir,

Thanks again for the call today — great context on the customer support routing pipeline and the latency expectation (~150ms p50 on short replies). Quick recap and a proposed next plan so we stay aligned: 

1) High-level fit: based on the volume (approx 8k tickets/day) and structured JSON output needs for downstream routing, we recommend evaluating two model families: an LLM optimized for structured output (opt-structured-1.3) and a lower-cost quantized variant (q-opt-structured-1.3-8bit) as a fallback. 

2) Benchmarks: attached is a one-pager with our recommended baselines and expected throughput/latency ranges (redwood_model_recs_and_benchmarks.pdf). We'll run a short targeted eval against your prompt set to validate schema compliance and regression risk.

3) Eval scope & success criteria:
   - JSON schema compliance: fields required by your routing service must be present and typed correctly (see prompt set).
   - Structured output stability: schema must be produced >98% on canonical prompts.
   - Retry/fallback semantics: if function/tool-calling fails (timeout/error), we want behavior: 1 retry with alternate model variant, then a deterministic fallback (static routing label) to avoid downstream failure.

4) Proposed next steps (action items):
   - You: send the canonical prompt set and a sample of 500 tickets (anonymized) — thank you for the prompt set attached here already (storlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).
   - Us (Redwood): run an initial schema compliance run (JSON schema tests + token/latency summary) and share CSV results + failing example prompts.
   - Joint: sync on policy for retries & fallbacks; if you want we can sketch the exact retry/backoff table.

Attachments in this thread: storlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, redwood_model_recs_and_benchmarks.pdf

I’ve CC’d Samir for procurement timing (if model commit/Dedicated capacity looks needed) — Samir, are there any budget windows we should know about?

Available for a quick 30-min follow-up Tues/Wed next week to walk the initial results.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ana Morales <ana@storlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — recommended models, schema tests, and next steps

Thanks Dylan — this is perfect. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For schema compliance, we have two routing fields: 
   - route_label (string, required)
   - priority_score (number, optional)
We also want confidence_score (0-1 float) for downstream throttling. Can you include those in the validator?

2) Regarding retries: our platform needs deterministic fallback in <= 250ms additional latency. If the model times out, is the retry on a different model variant handled by Redwood automatically, or should we implement client-side fallback logic?

I'll review the benchmark one-pager and we can share a small set of annotated tickets tomorrow. Attaching the prompt set export we used last quarter (storlytics_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — let me know if you need a different format.

Folks — forwarding Ana's reply and the prompt set. Can you help run a focused model-fit eval and JSON schema compliance check? Quick asks: 

- Dev: run opt-structured-1.3 and q-opt-structured-1.3-8bit on the 500-sample (first pass) for schema compliance; produce an eval CSV with per-prompt fields: prompt_id, model, schema_pass (true/false), missing_fields, confidence_score, token_cost, latency_ms. Attach eval_results_initial.csv. Also run a small tool-calling test: have the model emit a function call-like JSON payload and validate that our schema validator flags malformed fields.

- Grace: can you validate expected throughput impact on Dedicated versus Hosted with these models? We need a ballpark for 99th percentile latency under 10 concurrent requests and for the batched path.

Priority: get initial CSV and 10 failing examples back by EOD tomorrow so we can iterate with the customer. I dropped a short template at https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/schema-eval-template for the CSV headers.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-14T13:10:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Discovery recap — recommended models, schema tests, and next steps

All — initial run complete and attached (eval_results_initial.csv, schema-validator-tests.zip). Quick summary of findings: 

- opt-structured-1.3: schema_pass = 0.945 overall (out of 500 prompts). Most common failures: missing confidence_score (mostly null returned as empty string) and occasional priority_score returned as string instead of number. Median latency (hosted) = 138ms, p95 = 270ms; token_cost ~0.42 units/response.

- q-opt-structured-1.3-8bit: schema_pass = 0.895. Lower token_cost (~0.28) and improved median latency (120ms) but slightly more malformed numeric fields.

- Tool-calling test: when forcing a simulated timeout, the model sometimes emits partial JSON (truncated) — our validator flags these as malformed. I included 10 failing examples in the CSV. For retries: implementing server-side retry with an alternate model variant reduced malformed-rate by ~60% in synthetic tests (we retried once immediately on model error). However this added median extra latency of ~90ms on retry cases.

Attachments: eval_results_initial.csv (CSV, 1.1MB) — contains prompt_id,model,schema_pass,missing_fields,confidence_score,token_cost,latency_ms; schema-validator-tests.zip (examples and small harness)

Next steps I recommend:
- Add a small wrapper that checks schema immediately after generation and triggers one automatic retry on alternate model. If still malformed, emit deterministic fallback routing (static_label = "manual_review") and include a failure code in the output.
- Normalize numeric fields via a post-process step to coerce strings to numbers where safe; flag otherwise.

I'll schedule a short sync with Ana and Samir to review failing examples unless you want me to iterate first.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
